questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses three pairs of corresponding sides?

feedback.text: SSS stands for side-side-side, three corresponding side pairs.
SAS uses two sides and the included angle.
ASA uses two angles and the included side.
HL applies only to right triangles.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two sides and the included angle?

feedback.text: SSS has three side pairs.
SAS uses two corresponding sides and the angle between them.
AAS uses two angles and a non-included side.
AAA does not prove congruence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two angles and the included side?

feedback.text: AAS uses a non-included side.
SAS uses two sides and the included angle.
ASA uses two angles and the side between them.
SSA is not a valid congruence criterion in this lesson.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.1

Which criterion uses two angles and a non-included side?

feedback.text: ASA requires the side between the two angles.
SSS uses three side pairs.
HL is for right triangles.
AAS uses two angles and a side not between them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: GEO_U03_L04_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.GEO.TRI.3

Why can valid triangle congruence criteria be connected to rigid transformations?

answer.text: They change side lengths until two triangles match.

feedback.text: Rigid transformations do not change side lengths. They preserve distances while mapping one figure onto another.

answer.text: They rely only on the triangles looking the same.

feedback.text: Appearance is not proof. Congruence criteria give mathematical evidence that supports a rigid-motion match.

answer.text: They prove only that corresponding angles are equal.

feedback.text: Some angle information may be involved, but triangle congruence also requires enough evidence to fix size and shape.

answer.text: They provide enough evidence to map one triangle exactly onto the other.

feedback.text: Correct. Valid congruence criteria give enough side and angle information to justify that a rigid transformation can map one triangle exactly onto the other.
